name: Waterfront Public Access Areas (WPAAs)
description: Waterfront Public Access Areas (WPAAs) are privately owned waterfront zoning lots where publicly accessible open space is provided to and along the shoreline for public enjoyment, as shown on the Waterfront Access Map (WAM).

columns.name: the_geom
columns.description: Geometry type

columns.name: WPAA_ID
columns.description: A unique ID for each Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA). FKA PAWS ID - Publicly Accessible Waterfront Spaces ID.

columns.name: Name
columns.description: The name of the Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA)

columns.name: Construction Status
columns.description: The construction status of the Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA), it will be one of the following options: Approved (to be consutrcted), Open, Partially Open, Under Construction

columns.name: Chair Certification Date
columns.description: The date of Chair Certification associated with the creation of the Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA), if applicable.

columns.name: CPC Approval Date
columns.description: The date of City Planning Commission (CPC) approval associated with the creation of the Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA), if applicable.

columns.name: Maintained By
columns.description: The entity responsible for the maintenance of the Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA). It is typically: Private Property Owned, but may also be: NYC DPR or NYC EDC

columns.name: Summary of WPAA
columns.description: A general, 1-2 sentence descriptive overview of the Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA) highlighting key features

top.item: Waterfront open space with shore public walkway, supplemental public access area and street end improvement
A shore public walkway on the East River with seating, lighting, trees, and plantings.
Waterfront esplanade with a shore public walkway connecting to 2.5 miles of greenspace in conjunction with a three-tower development.

Walkway with seating, lighting and plantings on the Eastchester Bay of the Long Island Sound in conjunction with the development of a two story eating/drinking establishment pursuant to the Special City Island District zoning regulations
Waterfront walkway with landscaping and sitting areas along Pugsley Creek and the East River in conjunction with a 1,183- unit residential development.
Waterfront access including a shore public walkway with active and passive recreational activities on the East River, in conjunction with the mixed-use redevelopment of the former Domino Sugar site.
Visual corridors and public access easement in conjunction with the development of 25 one- and two-family houses at Raritan Bay.
Shore public walkway on the Flushing River with seating, lighting, trees, plantings, and upland connections in conjunction with a mixed-use residential and retail development.
Shore public walkway with seating, trees, lighting, visual corridors and upland connections on the East River in conjunction with a mixed use development in Astoria.
1.2 mile walkway with seating and lighting around the perimeter of four piers overlooking the Hudson River with viewing area, in conjunction with the development of Chelsea Piers recreation center

Public access easement to a waterfront esplanade on Lemon Creek of the Great Kills Harbor which also connects Lemon Creek Park to Wolfe's Pond Park in conjunction with the development of 118 one- and two-family houses.
A shore public walkway and landscaped public access area approved in conjunction with a mixed use residential and commercial development.

Shore public walkway with a boardwalk, seating area and a planted buffer area on the East River in conjunction with the residential development. This site is now owned by the NYC Dept. of Parks and Recreation.
Pedestrian path on the East River, visual corridors and a network of circulation paths, seating, and extenstive plantings in conjunction with a residential development.
Visual corridors and shore public walkway with trees, lighting and seating on Mill Basin in conjunction with the development of a retail store.
Shore public walkway, supplemental public access area and visual corridors, with seating, trees and lighting on Lower New York Bay in conjunction with an enlargement of an existing nursing home.

Upland connections, visual corridors, and a shore public walkway with seating, trees, lighting and an additional public open space provided on a portion of a roof overlooking the East River in conjunction with a mixed-use development.
Waterfront open space with shore public walkway and a Type 1 Upland Connection
Publicly accessible pier at the foot of India Street on the East River serving as a ferry stop with lighting and seating.

Future New York City DEP CSO facility will incorporate a community-driven waterfront public access design that will feature a variety of public amenities, open spaces, and educational uses alongside tidal restoration.

columns.name: Restrictive Declaration Link
columns.description: The hyperlink to or ID number of the restrictive declaration document on Dept. of Finanace's (DOF) Automated City Register Information System (ACRIS) webiste, associated with the creation of the Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA), if applicable.

columns.name: CPC Report Link
columns.description: The hyperlink to the City Planning Commission (CPC) Report associated with the creation of the Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA), if applicable.

columns.name: Supplemental Public Access Area
columns.description: Total supplemental public access area in square feet. Supplemental public access area is a public access area required in order to fulfill the minimum percentage of Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA)required on a waterfront zoning lot, once a shore public walkway and upland connection have been provided.

columns.name: Total WPAA Area
columns.description: Total Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA) in square feet. WPAA area is the portion of a waterfront zoning lot where publicly accessible open space is provided to and along the shoreline.

columns.name: Zoning Application Portal (ZAP) Link
columns.description: The hyperlink to the project in the Zoning Application Portal (ZAP) associated with the Waterfront Public Access Area (WPAA), if applicable.

columns.name: Hours of Operation
columns.description: Public hours of operation for Waterfront Public Access Areas (WPAAs). It is often Dawn to Dusk, but some WPAAs have seasonal differences in the times they are open.
